battle.name: 希臘獨立戰爭
battle.theater: 希臘本土、摩里亞與愛琴海
battle.brief: 一八二一年三月起，希臘起義在摩里亞與愛琴海同時爆發，把奧斯曼在希臘的守軍與艦隊拖入八年消耗戰；一八二七年十月二十日納瓦里諾海戰摧毀奧埃艦隊，一八二九年君士坦丁堡議和。西班牙方陣盾早已退下戰場，但它代表的密集橫排與整列齊射，正是希臘正規軍自一八二二年由法德教官引入的作戰基礎。

kit.name: 西班牙方陣盾
kit.history: 一面方盾撐住一整排人。無敵兵團的方陣靠它，也靠後面那排火繩槍。

countries: 這場戰爭是希臘起義者對奧斯曼帝國及受其節制的埃塞俄比亞的八年戰爭，交戰雙方在編制、訓練與後勤上分屬兩個世界。希臘一方最上層是「友誼會」這類秘密會社：一八一四年在敖德薩成立，到二一年已把敖德薩、君士坦丁堡、維也納與摩里亞的港口連成一張網，參加者多為受過西式教育的商人與軍官。一八二一年三月初，亞歷山大·伊普西蘭蒂率「聖隊」渡過普魯特河，在摩爾多瓦與瓦拉幾亞募兵，這支部隊在斯庫萊尼被殲滅；真正的全境起義則在四月的復活節於薩洛納與帕特雷一帶的修道院同時舉起黑底白十字旗，五月之後魯梅利亞、塞薩利與摩里亞先後響應。地面部隊分兩層：一層是各地武裝大隊，klepht 與 armatoloi 出身，人數以萬計而裝備雜亂；一層是常備的「陸軍」（Ελληνικόν Πεζικόν），一八二二年由巴伐利亞上校卡爾·威廉·馮·海德克按歐洲線列步兵條例整編，一八二五年後再由法國與德國教官重訂「方陣」編制，每個方陣由八個營組成，前四營列陣、後四營預備，炮兵置於中央，輜重與傷員收在陣內。附屬兵力包括七島共和國的愛希軍團（Philhellene Legion），由義大利上校德·法布里斯率領，後由法國人法維耶接掌，一八二一年在比薩一役全軍覆沒；還有米奧利斯在海德拉島率領的希臘艦隊，以及由商船與走私船改裝的武裝船隊。政權自一八二一年維斯提察與阿斯特羅斯大會起步，宗主教日耳曼努斯在金角灣法納爾升起紅底黑十字旗，一八二二年埃皮達魯斯會議頒布憲法，設立行政機構與立法議會，政權先後遷往特雷贊、哈尼亞、克里特，終於落腳納瓦里諾；一八二七年列強在倫敦議定由卡波迪斯特里亞斯出任攝政。奧斯曼一方由君士坦丁堡直接調度：蘇丹馬哈茂德二世平定埃及易卜拉欣之亂後回師，先誅阿里帕夏，再解散希臘人 armatoloi 的武裝與世襲職位，這兩道命令把人直接推向起義。總督級帕夏分掌摩里亞、埃比亞、魯梅利亞各區與希臘境內的特里波利察要塞，海軍由卡普丹帕夏統率，陸軍以歐洲式操典的安納托盧團與魯梅利亞團為骨幹，並倚賴大量非正規的土耳其與阿爾巴尼亞武裝。真正的轉折來自埃及：一八二五年易卜拉欣帕夏率約兩萬人的分遣隊渡海登陸摩里亞，這支按歐洲條例訓練、編有野戰炮兵並以阿爾巴尼亞突騎兵補充的部隊，其先鋒同年五月先攻下斯法克特里亞島，隨後兵臨科林斯，一八二六年包圍米索隆吉；一八二八年三月英法俄聯軍在摩里亞登陸，迫使易卜拉欣放棄摩里亞撤回埃及，奧斯曼在希臘的戰爭至此全面崩解。
countriesEn: This was an eight-year war fought by Greek insurgents against the Ottoman Empire and its dependent Egyptian province, and the two sides belonged to entirely different worlds of organisation, training and logistics. At the top of the Greek side stood secret societies of the Filiki Eteria type: founded at Odessa in 1814, by 1821 they had woven a single network through Odessa, Constantinople, Vienna and the ports of the Morea, and their members were largely merchants and officers with a Western education. In early March 1821 Alexander Ypsilantis led the Sacred Band across the Pruth and raised men in Moldavia and Wallachia, only for the band to be annihilated at Skuleni; the real rising over the whole country came on at Easter in April, when the monasteries around Salona and Patras raised the black flag with the white cross, and in May and after that Rumelia, Thessaly and the Morea answered in turn. The land forces had two layers: irregular bands raised by klephts and armatoloi, numbering in the thousands but wildly varied in equipment; and the standing army, the Ellinikon Pezikon, first reorganised on European line infantry lines by the Bavarian Colonel Karl Wilhelm von Heideck in 1822 and re-drafted by French and German instructors after 1825 under the phalanx system, each phalanx of eight battalions with four in front and four in reserve, the guns in the centre and the baggage and wounded kept inside the formation. Attached to it were the Philhellene Legion of the Septinsular Republic, commanded by the Italian Colonel de Fabris and later by the Frenchman Fabvier, destroyed at Peta in 1821; the Greek fleet under Miaoulis at Hydra; and a flotilla of merchantmen and smuggling craft converted into armed vessels. The polity began with the assemblies of Vostitsa and Astros in 1821: the Metropolitan Germanus raised the red flag with the black cross at the Phanar on the Golden Horn, the Epidaurus assembly of 1822 promulgated a constitution and set up an executive and a legislature, and the seat of government moved in turn to Troezen, Chania and Crete before settling at Navarino; in 1827 the powers meeting in London agreed that Capodistrias would serve as regent of Greece. The Ottoman side was directed from Constantinople: after Sultan Mahmud II had suppressed the revolt of Ibrahim in Egypt he turned back, executed Ali Pasha, and then disbanded the armatoloi of the Greeks together with their hereditary offices, two orders that pushed men straight into the rising. Pashas of governor rank held the different districts of the Morea, Epirus and Rumelia together with the fortress of Tripolitsa in Greece, the fleet was under the Kapudan Pasha, and the army rested on the European-drilled Anatolian and Rumelian regiments backed by large numbers of irregular Turkish and Albanian bands. The real turning point came from Egypt: in 1825 Ibrahim Pasha carried over a detachment of about twenty thousand men and landed in the Morea, and this force, trained on European lines, furnished with field artillery and reinforced by Albanian light horse, first took the island of Sphacteria and then closed on Corinth, besieging Missolonghi in 1826; when the British, French and Russian contingents landed in the Morea in March 1828 Ibrahim was forced to abandon the Morea and withdraw to Egypt, and the Ottoman war in Greece collapsed completely.
people: 核心人物分屬三個群體。希臘一方的武裝領袖以科洛科特羅尼斯為首：這位生於埃比亞扎戈里山區、被稱為「希臘人的元帥」的人，一八二二年在科林斯奪取阿克羅科林斯山堡，一八二六年在拉里薩擊敗穆斯塔法帕夏的縱隊，一八二八年隨聯軍進軍，隨後主持新國家的建制，是「軍隊」與「國家」兩端最長的黏合劑。海軍方面，米奧利斯在海德拉組織艦隊，以帆法與速度攔截奧軍運輸船隊；卡納里斯則以縱火快艇在希臘史上最出名的兩把火聞名——一八二一年四月十一日奇奧斯島外火攻奧軍旗艦並將其焚燬——其後出任海軍大臣與議會議長。米索隆吉的守將馬克里揚尼斯後來寫下《一個希臘人的回憶錄》，成為這場戰爭最重要的一手記錄，同城的武裝首領卡姆蘇洛斯則是出身教士的將領。內陸方面，卡拉伊斯卡基斯率領魯梅利亞的正規大隊，科萊蒂斯與察韋拉斯分別掌握阿卡納尼亞與利瓦季亞的武裝，察韋拉斯是阿爾巴尼亞裔的希臘首領，其「埃夫佐內」營日後成為希臘陸軍的骨幹；安德魯佐斯兼掌艦隊與政務。阿克羅科林斯的教區長日耳曼努斯以一八二一年在法納爾升旗、率領代表赴君士坦丁堡、主持一八二二年憲法會議而居功；卡波迪斯特里亞斯出身科爾島、在俄國與法國受過外交訓練，一八二七年出任攝政，一八三一年在希臘遇刺身亡。志願者之中，義大利人德·法布里斯、法國人法維耶、英國人赫斯廷斯與邱奇、德國人海德克與法國人德·里尼，把歐洲式操典帶進希臘；拜倫勳爵於一八二四年在米索隆吉組織救援隊並在同年病逝。奧斯曼與埃及方面的關鍵人物是蘇丹馬哈茂德二世、摩里亞總督穆薩·卡津、埃比亞總督奧梅爾·弗里奧尼、特里波利察的穆斯塔法帕夏、卡普丹帕夏，以及穆罕默德·阿里之子易卜拉欣；一八二七年十月二十日納瓦里諾海戰的指揮權分屬英國科德林頓、法國德·里尼與俄國海登。數百名遠道而來的志願者之中，真正影響戰局者幾乎全在上述名單之內。
peopleEn: The central figures fall into three groups. On the Greek side the military leader was Kolokotronis: born in the Zagori mountains of Epirus and called the marshal of the Greeks, he seized the Acrocorinth at Corinth in 1822, destroyed the column of Mustafa Pasha at the battle of Lariassa in 1826, marched in with the allied force in 1828 and then presided over the institutions of the new state, and he was the longest lasting link between the army and the country. At sea Miaoulis built a fleet at Hydra and used sail and speed to intercept Ottoman supply shipping; Kanaris is remembered for the two fires that made him famous, setting a fireship against the Ottoman flagship off Chios on 11 April 1821 and burning her out, and later serving as minister of the navy and speaker of the assembly. Makriyannis, the commander of Missolonghi, left behind the Memoirs of a Greek, the single most valuable eyewitness record of the war, while Koumoundouros, who led the same garrison, was a general who had been a priest. Inland, Karaiskakis led the regular bands of Rumelia, Kolettis and Tzavelas held the armed men of Acarnania and Livadia, Tzavelas being an Albanian-born Greek chief whose Evzones later became the backbone of the Greek army, and Androutsos commanded ships and government at once. Germanus, the hieromonk of the Acrocorinth, earned his place by raising the flag at the Phanar in 1821, leading the deputation to Constantinople and presiding over the constitutional assembly of 1822; Capodistrias, born on Corfu and trained as a diplomat in Russia and France, became regent in 1827 and was assassinated in Greece in 1831. Among the volunteers, the Italian de Fabris, the Frenchman Fabvier, the British Hastings and Church, the German Heideck and the Frenchman de Rigny carried European drill into Greece; Lord Byron organised the relief corps at Missolonghi in 1824 and died of fever there in the same year. On the Ottoman and Egyptian side the key men were Sultan Mahmud II, Musa Kazim Pasha, governor of the Morea, Omer Vrioni, governor of Epirus, Mustafa Pasha of Tripolitsa, the Kapudan Pasha, and Ibrahim, son of Muhammad Ali; command at Navarino on 20 October 1827 was shared by Codrington for Britain, de Rigny for France and Heyden for Russia. Of the hundreds of volunteers who came to Greece, the few who actually shaped the war are almost all to be found on this list.
kits: 本卡兵器是十六世紀西班牙方陣使用的方陣盾（tarache 與 pavés 兩種形制）：前者是直徑半米上下、蒙皮包鐵的圓盾，後者是高及胸口的大方盾，火繩槍手在行軍時舉盾成列，把火槍藏在盾後，接近敵陣後再放下作齊射。方陣盾在一八二一年早已不是戰場裝備：西班牙本土的 tercios 在一八〇二至一八〇五年的軍制改革中改為線列營，最後的 tercios 只餘加勒比與菲律賓的守備單位，方盾只在軍械庫、教練場與儀仗隊中作為遺物存在。它留在這場戰爭裡的位置，是作為一套組織法的標本：tercio 的血統是由「排」構成的連續橫排，火槍手居前排或後排同時射擊，遇騎兵衝鋒則閉合成四面方陣，槍盾相結、密度即為防力。希臘人一八二二年由海德克與法維耶引入的正是這套歐洲步兵操典，而一八二五年後法國教官手訂的方陣條例把八個營排成空心方陣、炮兵置中，更把閉合方陣的抗騎兵功能寫成明文規定，因此方陣盾雖未出現在希臘，它所代表的那面牆貫穿了整場戰爭。實際出現在希臘戰場上的裝備另有其物。希臘正規步兵多裝舊式燧發滑膛長槍（希臘人稱 kariofili），線列四排，配刺刀；一八二七年之後法國方面開始供應擊發式新槍，摩里亞守軍與希臘軍在納瓦里諾前後完成換裝。炮兵是六磅與八磅的輕型野戰炮，銅砲以牛或騾牽引；米索隆吉與摩里亞各堡靠城牆上架設的火砲與守備艦隊支援，海上有「塞薩利」與「赫拉克勒斯」兩艘武裝汽船，以及後來自美國購得的巡防艦「基多尼亞」與「忒爾普西科爾」，縱火快艇則是希臘海軍最廉價的重裝手段。游擊隊使用滑膛短手槍、彎刀、匕首與投石索，騎兵極少。奧斯曼陸軍以歐洲式燧發滑膛槍配刺刀為主，火炮為十二磅與六磅加農炮，攻城另備二十四磅攻城砲與臼砲，海軍以大帆船、巡防艦與數百艘划槳戰船組成。埃及分遣軍的裝備最為齊整：尼齊姆式步兵、十二磅砲與配屬騎兵砲隊，使其在野戰中遠勝希臘臨時拼湊的部隊。志願軍方面，愛希軍團與法國支隊配法式火槍與刺刀，後來的聯軍海陸戰隊裝備英法製線列步槍、刺刀與輕野戰砲。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the shield of the sixteenth-century Spanish tercia, in its two forms, the tarache and the pavés: the first a round buckler of some half a metre across, faced with iron over a wooden core, the second a large square shield standing as high as a man's chest, carried by the arquebusiers as they marched, the musket hidden behind it and the volley delivered once the enemy was in range. By 1821 the tercia shield was no longer a weapon of the field: the Spanish tercios on the peninsula were converted into line battalions in the reforms of 1802 to 1805, and only the fixed garrison units in the Caribbean and the Philippines remained, so that the shield survived in arsenals, on drill grounds and in ceremonial columns as a relic. The place it holds in this war is as the model of a method of organisation. The bloodline of the tercio was the continuous line of ranks, musketeers in the front or rear rank firing simultaneously, closing into a hollow square against a cavalry charge, musket and shield locked together so that density was the defence. What the Greeks imported in 1822 through Heideck and Fabvier was precisely this European infantry drill, and the phalanx regulations written by French instructors after 1825 turned the anti-cavalry square into a written rule, eight battalions hollowed out with the guns in the middle, so the shield never appeared in Greece but the wall it stood for ran through the whole war. The equipment actually on the Greek battlefield was of another kind. Greek regular infantry carried old flintlock smoothbore muskets, known to the Greeks as kariofili, drawn up in four ranks with bayonets, and after 1827 the French began supplying percussion muskets, so that the garrisons of the Morea and the Greek army completed their re-armament around the time of Navarino. The artillery was light field guns of six and eight pounds, bronze pieces drawn by oxen or mules; the garrisons of Missolonghi and the fortresses of the Morea relied on guns mounted on the ramparts and on the support of their garrison fleets, and at sea there were the gunboats Thessaly and Hercules and the frigates Kydonia and Terpsichore, bought in the United States, while the fireship remained the cheapest form of heavy punch available to the Greek navy. The irregulars used smoothbore pistols, sabres, daggers and slings, and they had very little cavalry. The Ottoman infantry was armed mainly with European flintlock muskets and bayonets, the artillery with twelve and six pounders, siege with twenty-four pounders and mortars, and the navy was built of galleasses, corvettes and several hundred galleys. The Egyptian detachment was the best equipped of all: Nizam infantry, twelve pounders and an attached horse battery gave it a clear edge over the Greek army in the field. On the volunteer side the Philhellene Legion and the French auxiliary corps carried French muskets and bayonets, and the later allied marine and land detachments were equipped with British and French line muskets, bayonets and light field guns.
tactics: 希臘人的戰術起於一場不對稱的包圍。起義初期沒有能力攻城奪堡，便以游擊大隊切斷奧軍在摩里亞與魯梅利亞的交通線，燒毀田禾以斷糧秣，圍困帕特雷、特里波利察、納夫普利翁以及被稱為摩里亞兩隻眼睛的莫登與科羅尼，還有扼守科林斯海口的布爾齊碉堡，使分散的守軍無法互相支援，再由常備大隊在外圍與奧軍野戰隊正面交鋒。一八二二年組建政權與徵兵之後，戰術轉向分進合擊：科洛科特羅尼斯在科林斯、馬克里揚尼斯在西部海峽、卡拉伊斯卡基斯在魯梅利亞三線同時發動，迫使奧軍在三個方向上分兵。步兵的核心是方陣：面對阿爾巴尼亞輕騎兵的衝鋒，希臘人閉合成四面有刺刀的方牆，以火槍輪射與刺刀牆硬吃衝鋒；一八二五年後的方陣條例把這套做法制度化，同時要求作戰時散開為散兵線，每營散兵在前面遮蔽、主力營在後待命，炮兵分列兩翼，梯隊推進。海上的戰術更趨近於襲擊。希臘艦隊沒有能力與奧軍巡防艦正面決鬥，便以縱火快艇衝擊停泊中的大帆船，一八二一年奇奧斯島外與一八二四年薩摩斯外海各得手一次；同時以數十艘小艇封鎖海峽，騷擾奧軍運兵船與糧船，迫使奧軍在陸戰失利後無法由海路增兵。一八二七年聯軍到場後，戰術改為海上封鎖加登陸：英法俄三國分遣隊在摩里亞南部登陸，與希臘正規軍會合後攻向斯法克特里亞島與皮洛斯的堡壘線。納瓦里諾一役的佈陣是全戰最精密的一場：奧埃艦隊以新月形泊在納瓦里諾灣內，灣口狹窄而水淺，大型帆船無法迴旋；聯軍縱隊由西口進入，分兩列前進，領先艦越過敵列之後向右轉向，逐艦以縱射與橫射貫穿敵陣，形成橫穿T字的射擊，首輪齊射之後土耳其側的旗艦與主力艦相繼起火。戰後的摩里亞戰役中，聯軍海陸戰隊與希臘人合圍斯法克特里亞島上的埃及軍工事，再以縱隊登陸作戰，迫使易卜拉欣放棄摩里亞。
tacticsEn: The Greek way of war began as an unequal encirclement. In the first phase they had no means of taking the fortresses, so irregular bands cut the Ottoman communications in the Morea and Rumelia, burned crops to starve the garrisons, and invested Patras, Tripolitsa and Nafplion together with Methoni and Koroni, the two coastal strongholds called the two eyes of the Morea, and the fort of Bourtzi that guarded the entrance to the Gulf of Corinth, so that the isolated garrisons could not support one another, while the regular bands met the Ottoman field army in the open outside. After a polity and a levy had been organised in 1822 the tactics turned to converging attacks on three axes: Kolokotronis in the Corinth area, Makriyannis in the western straits and Karaiskakis in Rumelia struck at the same time, forcing the Ottomans to divide in three directions. The heart of the infantry was the square: faced with the charge of Albanian light horse, the Greeks closed into a wall of bayonets on four faces and absorbed the charge with volleys of musket fire and steel, and the phalanx regulations after 1825 put this practice on paper, while also requiring the army to deploy into a skirmish line, with the skirmishers of each battalion in front and the main body waiting behind, the guns on the two wings and the advance made in echelon. At sea the tactics came closer to the raid. The Greek fleet had no strength to meet the Ottoman corvettes in a set battle, so it used fireships against great ships lying at anchor, once off Chios in 1821 and once off Samos in 1824, and at the same time a few dozen small craft blockaded the straits and harassed the Ottoman troop and provision ships, cutting off the sea reinforcement of the Ottoman army once it had lost on land. When the allied squadrons arrived in 1827 the method changed to a naval blockade combined with landings: the British, French and Russian detachments landed in the south of the Morea, joined the Greek regular army and drove at the line of works on the island of Sphacteria and at Pylos. The deployment at Navarino was the most exact piece of work of the whole war: the Ottoman-Egyptian fleet lay in a crescent inside the bay, whose mouth was narrow and shallow, so that great ships could not manoeuvre; the allied column entered from the west in two divisions, the leading ships passed beyond the enemy line and then turned to starboard, firing longitudinal and raking broadsides down the anchored line in the form of a cross of the T, and after the first salvo the Turkish flagship and the ships next to her began to burn. In the campaigns that followed in the Morea, allied marines and land detachments closed with the Greeks around the Egyptian works on Sphacteria and then landed in column, and Ibrahim was forced to abandon the Morea.
data: 雙方兵力與損失的數字，來源分歧頗大，只能取大致量級。希臘方面：一八二一年參與起義的武裝人數以萬計，但真正有統一旗號與常備編制的正規軍在各來源中多被描述為數千人；一八二五年後按方陣編制重整，常備兵力估計在五千至一萬之間，其中海軍可用船隻數十艘，多為商船與走私船改裝，另有數艘巡防艦與武裝汽船。奧斯曼方面：一八二一年在希臘的陸軍與各路非正規武裝合計以萬計；一八二五年易卜拉欣分遣隊渡海，兵力在兩萬至兩萬五千之間，含阿爾巴尼亞騎兵與步兵師；到一八二六年，奧埃聯軍在摩里亞的總兵力被估計在三萬至四萬。海戰：納瓦里諾一戰，聯軍出動戰列艦二十七艘，分屬英、法、俄三國，各國艦數的說法略有出入而英國分遣隊規模最大，另有巡防艦與運輸船數十艘；奧埃方面的船隻在港內總數近百，實際列陣作戰的約六十至七十艘，多為划槳戰船。此役奧埃方面陣亡與受傷合計約三千至四千人，被俘約二千至二千五百人，六十餘艘戰船焚毀、擱淺或被俘獲，聯軍方面的傷亡在數百至近千人之間。米索隆吉：第一次圍城起於一八二二年，守軍與民兵合計數千人；第二次圍城起於一八二五年，守軍最後只剩數百人，另有數百名志願軍，一八二五年九月托馬斯·戈登率領的救援部隊在阿拉克索斯河畔的「大牆」一役被擊敗後退出戰場，一八二六年四月守軍點燃火藥庫全軍覆沒。時間與距離：起義自一八二一年三月至一八二九年九月，前後八年半；希臘正規軍自摩里亞向中希臘與西部推進的補給線多靠海運與騾隊，冬季行軍要穿越摩里亞南部的大沼澤地帶，遲滯與缺糧多次導致戰役失利。
dataEn: The figures for men and losses on both sides differ widely from source to source, and only the rough order of magnitude can be given. On the Greek side: the number of men who took up arms in 1821 runs into the tens of thousands, but the regular army with a common standard and a standing establishment is described by most sources as numbering in the several thousands; after the reorganisation on the phalanx system in 1825 the permanent force is estimated at between five and ten thousand men, of which the navy had several dozen usable vessels, mostly converted merchantmen and smuggling craft, plus a few frigates and armed steamers. On the Ottoman side: the troops stationed in Greece in 1821, together with the irregular bands, together ran to tens of thousands; the Egyptian detachment that crossed the sea in 1825 numbered between twenty and twenty-five thousand men including Albanian cavalry and infantry; by 1826 the total Ottoman-Egyptian force in the Morea was estimated at thirty to forty thousand. At sea, in the battle of Navarino the allies brought twenty-seven ships of the line, divided between Britain, France and Russia, the exact allocation being reported differently but the British detachment the largest, with several dozen frigates and transports besides; the Ottoman-Egyptian vessels numbered close to a hundred in the bay, of which sixty to seventy were engaged in the line, mostly galleys. In that battle the Ottoman-Egyptian side lost about three to four thousand men killed and wounded and had some two to two and a half thousand taken prisoner, sixty-odd ships were burned, stranded or captured, and the allied casualties ran from several hundred to close on a thousand. For Missolonghi: the first siege began in 1822 with several thousand defenders and militia; the second began in 1825, when the garrison was finally reduced to several hundred men with several hundred volunteers, and after Thomas Gordon's relief force was defeated in the action at the Great Walls by the Araxos in September 1825 it withdrew from the field, and in April 1826 the garrison fired the powder magazines and the whole body perished. In time and distance: the rising ran from March 1821 to September 1829, a little over eight years; the supply line of the Greek regular army as it pushed from the Morea towards central and western Greece rested mainly on sea transport and mule teams, and winter marches had to cross the great marshes in the south of the Morea, where delay and want of food were repeatedly decisive.
cause: 起義的成因有三層。最下層是奧斯曼對巴爾幹基督徒的結構性壓力：希臘正教教會受蘇丹直接管轄，教產屢遭沒收，主教與僧侶受審問，商人與航運受到嚴格管制；一八二〇年蘇丹馬哈茂德二世下令解散希臘人 armatoloi 的武裝與世襲職位，等於把一支本已刀口舐血的希臘地方武力逼入地下，摩里亞的 klepht 隨即轉為公開起義。一八二一年三月君士坦丁堡的宗主教區遭到清洗，總主教西里爾·盧卡里斯在同年被處決，宗教界也沒有退路。中層是知識層的組織與思想準備：友誼會自一八一四年起在敖德薩成立，得到希臘散居商人、莫斯科大學的希臘學生與俄國軍官的支援；一八二〇年西班牙的自由革命與義大利那不勒斯的革命又給了自由派示範，秘密會社的網絡把歐洲與巴爾幹的愛國者連在一起。伊普西蘭蒂在多瑙尼亞的計畫原本是一場以俄國軍官為核心、假借沙皇名義的軍事政變，起義蔓延到希臘本土之後，它變成一場真正的民族起義。最上層是帝國內部的連鎖崩解：一八二〇年易卜拉欣在埃及自立，馬哈茂德二世平叛後收緊中央控制，卻同時失去對巴爾幹的間接控制；阿爾巴尼亞武裝在南斯拉夫、希臘與安納托利亞同時被大量起用，把帝國邊境變成焦土。希臘起義恰好落在帝國最不能承受兵力的時點：蘇丹正把主力壓在阿爾巴尼亞與亞細亞，可供希臘使用的海軍與援軍都有限。
causeEn: The outbreak had three layers of cause. The lowest was the structural pressure of the Ottomans on the Balkan Christians: the Greek Orthodox Church stood directly under the Sultan, church property was repeatedly confiscated, bishops and clergy were interrogated, and trade and shipping were tightly controlled; in 1820 Sultan Mahmud II ordered the disbanding of the armatoloi and of their hereditary offices, driving a Greek local force that was already ready to fight underground into hiding, and the klephts of the Morea turned at once to open revolt. In March 1821 the patriarchal quarter in Constantinople was purged, and the Patriarch Cyril Lucaris was executed in the same year, so that the Church had no retreat either. The middle layer was the organisation and the intellectual preparation: the Filiki Eteria, founded at Odessa in 1814, was supported by Greek merchants abroad, Greek students at Moscow University and Russian officers; the liberal revolutions in Spain and in Naples in 1820 gave the liberals their example, and the network of secret societies linked patriots across Europe and the Balkans. The plan of Ypsilantis in the Danubian principalities had originally been a military conspiracy of Russian officers under the borrowed name of the Tsar, and once the rising spread to Greece itself it turned into a genuine national insurrection. The upper layer was the chain of collapses inside the empire: Ibrahim had set himself up in Egypt in 1820, Mahmud II crushed that revolt and tightened central control while at the same time losing his indirect hold on the Balkans; Albanian bands were employed in large numbers in Serbia, Greece and Anatolia at once, turning the imperial frontier into a burnt zone. The Greek rising fell at the moment when the empire could least afford the men: the Sultan was pressing his strength towards Albania and Asia, and the ships and troops available for Greece were limited.
impact: 這場戰爭的結果不只是一個新國家出現。它把希臘人從奧斯曼的米利特編制裡抽出，第一次建立以民族、以憲法、以常備軍為骨架的近代國家機器：一八二二年埃皮達魯斯憲法是歐洲最早一批由革命議會制定的近代憲法之一，一八二七年特雷贊憲法設立參議院與明確的行政權，一八二八至一八二九年間卡波迪斯特里亞斯在摩里亞推行統一稅制、造幣、軍隊與土地政策，這套建國經驗在往後四十餘年裡被反覆引用。疆界則完全沒有達成起義者的目標：一八三〇年倫敦議定書只承認南方摩里亞、雅典與部分島嶼，塞薩利、埃比亞、克里特與馬其頓全部排除在外，這些地區此後陸續重演克里特起義、塞薩利戰爭與巴爾幹戰爭。一八二六年蘇丹廢除禁衛軍並建立新軍，一八二〇至一八三〇年代推行歐式兵制改革，起義的直接刺激是其中之一。國際層面，愛希運動第一次讓歐洲的公眾與知識界為一個非歐洲的國家募集金錢與兵員，德意志的銀行家、義大利的流亡者與俄國的軍官都曾直接參與；這套模式後來被用來支援波蘭、西班牙與義大利的起義，成為十九世紀歐洲民族主義的跨國網路。長期代價則是未解決的邊境衝突與其後的居民移徙，這些都是這場戰爭留下而沒有收場的問題。
impactEn: The result of this war was not only the appearance of a new state. It pulled the Greeks out of the Ottoman millet structure and built, for the first time, a modern state machine resting on nationality, on a constitution and on a standing army: the Epidaurus constitution of 1822 was among the earliest modern constitutions written by revolutionary assemblies in Europe; the Troezen constitution of 1827 established a senate and an explicit executive; and between 1828 and 1829 Capodistrias carried out a unified tax system, a coinage, army and land policy in the Morea, an experience in state building that was cited again and again for the next forty years and more. The frontiers were a different matter, and fell far short of what the insurgents had aimed at: the London Protocol of 1830 recognised only the southern Morea, Athens and part of the islands, while Thessaly, Epirus, Crete and Macedonia were left out, and over those regions the war was fought again and again in the Cretan revolt, the Thessalian campaign and the Balkan Wars. In 1826 the Sultan abolished the Janissaries and raised a new army, and the reforms of the European type carried through in the 1820s and 1830s were in part driven by the shock of this rising. At the international level, the Philhellenic movement was the first time that the European public and the European intellectual world raised money and men for a country outside Europe, with German bankers, Italian exiles and Russian officers all taking part directly; the model was later used to support the risings in Poland, Spain and Italy and became a transnational network of nineteenth-century European nationalism. The lasting cost was the unresolved border conflict that followed, and the population transfers that came later, both of them questions left open by this war.
result: 希臘一方在戰場上勝出，關鍵有三。其一，一八二七年十月二十日納瓦里諾海戰摧毀奧斯曼與埃及在愛琴海的主力，土耳其既不能由海路向摩里亞增兵，也失去對希臘沿海島嶼的制海權，縱火快艇的游擊從此失去對手。其二，一八二八年英法俄聯軍在摩里亞登陸，與希臘正規軍合流，易卜拉欣同年放棄摩里亞，特里波利察在五月二十三日投降，莫登、科羅尼與科林斯相繼易手，摩里亞全境落入希臘人手中。其三，一八二五年之後的方陣化改組與外籍教官的操典整頓，使希臘正規軍在裝備、指揮與後勤上足以承擔攻堅。戰爭以一八二九年九月十四日君士坦丁堡附近的阿德里安堡條約收場，蘇丹承認希臘為獨立國家，一八三〇年二月三日倫敦議定書由英、法、俄三國擔保這一結果。但戰果的邊界同樣明確：希臘人沒有拿回塞薩利、埃比亞、馬其頓與克里特，起義中最激烈的南部戰線換來的只是一個比運動目標小得多的國家；奧斯曼帝國在希臘問題上退回亞那托利亞，此後再沒有能力在巴爾幹重建強權。希臘人的軍事勝利也沒有帶來穩定的共和：卡波迪斯特里亞斯於一八三一年遇刺，一八三三年巴伐利亞的奧托被立為國王，軍隊與政黨之間的分裂延續到十九世紀中葉才逐步收束。方陣盾留給這場戰爭的東西則是一種已經過時卻仍在制度裡存活的組織記憶：當年西班牙人用一面盾撐住一整排人的辦法，一八二二年之後的希臘人用一整個營的方陣去重做。
resultEn: The Greeks won on the field, and three things explain it. First, the battle of Navarino on 20 October 1827 destroyed the main strength of the Ottoman and Egyptian fleets in the Aegean: the Turks could no longer reinforce the Morea by sea and lost the command of the Greek coastal islands, and the raids of the fireships found no opponent left. Second, in 1828 the British, French and Russian forces landed in the Morea and joined hands with the Greek regular army; Ibrahim abandoned the Morea in the same year, Tripolitsa surrendered on 23 May, and Methoni, Koroni and Corinth changed hands in turn, so that the whole Morea fell to the Greeks. Third, the reorganisation on the phalanx system after 1825 and the drill instruction given by the foreign instructors left the Greek regular army able, in equipment, command and logistics, to undertake a siege. The war closed with the Treaty of Adrianople, signed near Constantinople on 14 September 1829, in which the Sultan recognised Greece as an independent state, and the Protocol of London of 3 February 1830, by which Britain, France and Russia guaranteed the result. But the limits of the victory were equally plain: the Greeks recovered neither Thessaly, nor Epirus, nor Macedonia, nor Crete, and the southern front, where the fiercest fighting had taken place, bought a country far smaller than the one the movement had set out to win; the Ottoman Empire withdrew to Anatolia on the Greek question and was never able to rebuild its strength in the Balkans again. The military victory of the Greeks did not bring a stable republic either: Capodistrias was assassinated in 1831, Otto of Bavaria was made king in 1833, and the rift between army and party was not closed off until the middle of the nineteenth century. What the tercia shield left to this war was an organisational memory already obsolete yet still alive inside institutions: the way in which the Spaniards once held a whole rank behind a single shield was, after 1822, remade by the Greeks as a whole battalion closed into a square.
